title: ID0418357-DC/Si-D/BE-[Multi] CCV problem
description:
Reported behavior/issue:
I am required to create a ticket through this route for the CCV problems. Erik Bruin (Heliox) is our contact person for this. Following issues have already been discussed: As you know we are experiencing CCV problems with some chargers. Further investigation shows that there actually seem to be 3 different errors which all cause that the card cannot be used - message 'unauthorized license' - message 8E15 - terminal list empty

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0418357-DC/Unknown/BE-[N/A] CCV problem CRM:02679000087
additional_info.body:
Hi Vishal, see attached.
This was the initial email from the customer
Best,
Erik
Translation:
Good afternoon Erik, Martijn,
As you're aware, we're experiencing CCV problems with some chargers. Further investigation shows that there appear to be 3 different errors, all of which prevent payment processing:
• 'unauthorized license' message • '8E15' message • 'terminal list empty'
To provide clearer direction and assist you with the solution, I've had the chargers analyzed per error message.
This email concerns the 'unauthorized license' message.
It appears that in some cases, an incorrect modem is installed in the UFC. In the attachment, you can see an image of a modem where behind KEY there's a code containing the word PAYONE.
95% of the modems have CCV KBC written behind KEY, and the EPDC technicians can log in using special CCV/Siemens software to perform the configuration.
However, there are also some modems with the KEY 'PAYONE' and even 'CARDPROCES' in circulation (4 UFCs in total), and these cannot be logged into.
It seems that EPDC simply doesn't have access because the modem wasn't made for CCV. Upon inquiry, we learned of a previous case where Marnic replaced a modem, likely (though we didn't receive feedback on this) also involving a modem not intended for CCV.
My question is: How should we report this? Sparki can create a ticket, but I'm finding it difficult to explain the situation clearly. Is there an easier way to raise this issue? Perhaps a combination of a ticket and sending it to you @Bruin, Erik?

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0418357-DC/Unknown/BE-[N/A] CCV problem CRM:02679000087
additional_info.body:
Hi Erik/ Martijn,
We have got the feedback from the experts regarding "Terminal candidate list empty" issue.
They have suggested to:
Check, if right ports are used to connect COR A10 to OPM-C60.
Check cable connection between Processing Unit and Card Reader.
Re-connect cables and re-start charger.
Exchange COR A10.
Regarding 'unauthorized license' message • '8E15' message, they have not found anything related at the charger.
Thank you
Best Regards,
Vishal Dhiman
eMobility Support Team
